top_strength: The pricing and differentiator block was genuinely strong, and she sold on value instead of just reading rates. She caught that the customer's dates were flexible and turned it into savings: "if we will do a packing on the Thursday. That will be $104 per hour per mover, so we can save at least $12 per hour compared to a Friday or almost $15 per hour on a Saturday." She then landed all three differentiators by name - No Worries ("up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement"), Meet Your Mover ("we will send you their names ahead of time to let you know who's coming"), and the On-Time Guarantee ("if we run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts by the end of the day") - plus the no-hidden-fees pitch and the 2.5-hour minimum with a sense-check. Her probing was thorough too, including the school-bus walk-distance equivalent and a proactive box estimate ("usually we end up with forty to fifty boxes").
coaching_note: The close is where this call leaked the most points - 3 of 11 on Quote/Booking. When Christie said "Yeah, I wanna look at the email," Joanna accepted it and ended the call without a single one of the tools that turns an email into a booking: no "there's no deposit to lock it in," no walkthrough of what's bolded at the top of the email, no "reply with any corrections so I know I've got it right," no "any other questions before I let you go?", and no hours or callback info. Build one standard close and run it every time: no deposit, here's what's bolded, reply with corrections, any questions, here's how to reach us. Second gap: the Save Your Ass prep speech never happened, and she handed herself the perfect opening by saying "if you are planning to do the packing yourself it will be just half of it" - that $1,962 moment was the place to explain that consolidating toys, drawers, and wall photos and taking a carload shortens the move and lowers the bill.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and organized with light affirmations ("Okay, awesome!", "That's perfect"), but the warmth stays transactional - the customer answers almost entirely in one-word replies and no rapport moment or empathy statement ever lands.
